title: Mixed-Precision & Numerical Stability: NaNs, Accumulation, Scaling (Draft)
content:
Status: Draft
Authors: Marina Lopez (owner), Ethan Park, Priya Nair, Jamal Thompson
Purpose: Record investigation into mixed-precision numerical stability issues observed in the serving runtime (NaNs, infs, unexpected accumulation behavior) and propose mitigations at the kernel, scheduler, and KV-cache layers.

Summary / TL;DR:
- We observed intermittent NaNs and occasional divergence in token logits when serving models in FP16 (amp) on A100/V100 GPUs under high-concurrency workloads.
- Root causes appear to be a combination of: reduced dynamic range in FP16 for accumulation-heavy kernels (matmul/softmax/gelu), inconsistent scaling across fused kernels, and KV-cache state updates that expose tiny NaNs which get amplified during autoregressive decoding.
- Immediate mitigations: enable per-op accumulation in FP32 for matmuls above threshold, insert robust NaN checks at KV-cache writeback and decoding, and add automatic bias/ln clipping and residual scaling heuristics.
- Longer-term: refactor kernel fusion contracts to carry dtype & scale metadata, extend scheduler to tag latency-critical requests for more conservative numeric mode, and add comprehensive regression tests and synthetic stress harnesses.

Scope / Context:
- Applies to: serving-runtime inference path for autoregressive transformer models (decoder-only and encoder-decoder in decode loop), running on NVIDIA GPUs that support FP16/bfloat16. Also relevant to CPU inference paths if mixed-precision used.
- Not covering: training, quantized INT8/4 kernels (different failure modes), or model conversion issues outside runtime kernels.

Observed Failures & Repro Steps:
1) Symptom: Rare NaN in logits after 20-200 tokens of decoding on long-running sessions. Affected models: LLaMA-variant (13B), and one customer-open model (tested) at sequence lengths >1024 with KV-cache reuse.
   - Repro (semi-deterministic): Run batched decode with batch_size=16, concurrency=8, beam=1, temp=0.7, with mixed-precision enabled and continuous prefix cache across batches. After ~50k tokens served, NaNs appear in softmax inputs.
2) Symptom: Divergence vs FP32 baseline where FP16 returns apparently valid numbers but topk tokens differ and perplexity grows over long sequences. Not NaN but quality regression.
   - Repro: Deterministic seed version: single session, use fp16 kernels with fused attention. Compare token-by-token logits to fp32 run; drift accumulates after ~400 tokens.
3) Symptom: Infrequent Inf spikes caused by overflow in GELU/fused-activation when combined with large residual sums.

Investigation Notes (what we ran):
- Collected GPU error counters, nvprof traces, and recorded .pt exported kernels.
- Ran defender harness: stress_decode.py with variable batch/seq/concurrency on A100.
- Instrumented runtime to dump first NaN-containing tensor and KV-cache entries preceding NaN.
- Added per-op FP32 accumulation flags to matmul kernels and observed reduction in NaN frequency (~95% reduction) but ~1.6x token latency for those ops.

Root Cause Hypotheses (ordered):
1) Accumulation precision loss in FP16 GEMM (qk/v value accumulation and output) causes tiny rounding errors that lead to denormals and eventually underflow/overflow in subsequent softmax/exp. This is exacerbated by fused kernels that assume certain dynamic range and do not rescale intermediate accumulators.
2) Inconsistent scaling between fused kernels: e.g., a fused attention kernel applies a single scaling factor but upstream linear projection used a different implicit scale (mixed bfloat16/float16 codepaths), causing mismatch at boundary and temporary overflow.
3) KV-cache writeback: when caching key/value tensors in FP16, we observed sporadic NaNs in KV entries probably due to uninitialized memory reuse on some GPU kernels when dimension % warp_size != 0 (edge-case writes).
4) Autocast interactions: our higher-level autocast context sometimes allowed bfloat16 for some ops vs float16 for others; this mixed dtype within a block can create unexpected casting and accumulation that changes numerical path.

Key Experiments and Results:
- Experiment A: FP16 GEMM with FP32 accumulation vs FP16 accumulation
  Result: FP32 accum reduces NaNs dramatically; median latency increase for GEMM = +60%, tail increase larger for small matrices.
- Experiment B: Force bfloat16 for attention kernels on A100
  Result: bfloat16 improved dynamic range; NaNs frequency very low, latency comparable to FP16 in many ops, but model weights need conversion and not all kernels natively optimized for BF16 on older hardware.
- Experiment C: KV-cache NaN injection test (write/uninitialized)
  Result: When KV stride not aligned, certain custom kernels left slots unread leading to stale NaNs. Fixing zero-initialization removed ~30% of observed NaNs in stress runs.

Immediate Mitigations (low-hanging fruit):
- Runtime config flags (serve-side): numeric_stability_mode: off|warn|strict
  - warn: log first NaN and continue; strict: fail the request and fallback to FP32 path for that session.
- Kernel-level: enable FP32 accumulation for large GEMMs (threshold tunable by shape) and optionally for attention matmuls where seq_len * head_dim > N. Add microkernel path for FP16 accum -> FP32 accumulation accumulation->cast back to FP16.
- KV-cache: on allocation, zero-init memory pages for key and value caches. Add sanity checks on writeback (isfinite) with fast-path skip in perf builds.
- Autocast hygiene: audit and unify autocast to prefer a single mixed-precision policy per model: {prefer_bf16, prefer_fp16, prefer_fp32}. Avoid mixing bf16/fp16 in the same fused operator boundary.
- Softmax: use stable softmax (subtract max) in all fused attention kernels and add clip for inputs to exp() (e.g., clip to [-40, 40] or adaptive based on dtype).

Proposed Kernel Changes (medium effort):
- Contract metadata: every fused kernel should return a small header (dtype, pre_scale, post_scale) so downstream kernels understand scale. Keep header minimal (2 floats) and per-call, not per-buffer. This avoids implicit assumptions when composing fused ops in schedules.
- Atomic-safe KV-cache writes: ensure kernels writing to KV-cache use store primitives that avoid partial writes on misaligned sizes; fall back to element-wise write for tail elements.
- Deterministic accum path: optionally provide a deterministic FP32-accumulation path for regressed customers (configurable per deployment).

Scheduler / Serving Implications:
- Heuristic routing: add numeric_mode tag to request metadata. For high-SLO, low-latency customers prefer FP16 aggressive mode; for mission-critical or high-sequence tasks, route to conservative numeric_mode (bf16 or fp32-accum).
- Capacity planning: conservative numeric modes increase GPU token cost ~1.2-1.8x; costing model should capture this and enable per-customer default.
- Canary rollout: new kernel variants must be canaried with gradual traffic and metric checks for NaN rates, top-1/5 differences versus baseline, and token-level perplexity.

KV-cache specific recommendations:
- Store KV in the highest affordable precision that fits memory budget; prefer bf16 over fp16 when supported and when memory delta acceptable.
- Add a compact per-session checksum or small per-token validity byte to KV entries to quickly detect corruption/NaN before using them in matmul.
- When reloading from disk/network, always validate isfinite(KV) and optionally run a quick norm-check to detect drift.

Testing Strategy / Regression Suite:
- Synthetic stress harness: multi-session, multi-batch, long-run (>1M tokens) stress tests across GPU types (A100, H100, V100) with varying seq lengths and shapes.
- Golden baseline: run periodic token-by-token comparison vs FP32 baseline for small sample sessions. Flag when KL-divergence or topk mismatch surpass thresholds.
- Fault injection: inject denormals, NaNs, and partial writes into KV-cache to verify detection.
- Performance guardrails: measure median and p95 token latency for FP32-accum variants and compare to FP16 baseline; define acceptable tradeoffs.

Open Questions / Tradeoffs:
- BF16 vs FP16: BF16 reduces overflow issues while preserving speed on newer hardware, but not universally supported. Should we default to BF16 where available and fallback to FP16 with more aggressive accumulation?
- Per-op accumulation costs: is it acceptable to use FP32 accum for attention GEMMs but keep FP16 for projection matmuls to reduce token latency impact? Need microbenchmarks per-model.
- Memory cost of higher-precision KV-cache vs accuracy benefit: what's the sweet spot (e.g., store keys in bf16, values in fp16)?
- How often do NaNs/instabilities occur in real customer workloads vs stress harness? Current telemetry suggests <0.1% sessions but higher for long-running, high-seq workloads.

Action Items (owners & next steps):
- (Priya) Add zero-init and isfinite checks to KV-cache allocation and writeback. Deploy to staging. ETA: 2w.
- (Ethan) Implement FP32 accumulation microkernel for GEMM and add shape-based threshold config. Bench on A100/H100. ETA: 3w.
- (Marina) Update serving runtime autocast to explicit mode enum and add explicit policy per-model. ETA: 1w for API, 4w for rollout.
- (Jamal) Build stress harness and synthetic regression tests; add nightly runs on dedicated cluster. ETA: 2w for harness, 1mo for stable nightly.
- (Team) Define canary policy for numeric changes and add metrics: NaN rate, top-1 divergence, KL-divergence vs FP32 baseline.

Appendix: Quick reference of observed numeric heuristics
- Clip exp inputs to [-40, 40] for FP16 softmax (tunable).
- Use FP32 accumulation when (seq_len * head_dim) > 32768 (empirical).
- Prefer BF16 on A100/H100 when model weights converted and kernel path optimized.
- Zero-init KV-cache pages on allocation and validate isfinite on readback in debug builds.

Notes / rough logs (raw):
- 2025-11-20: first customer report of NaNs under long-run session (prod).
- 2025-11-21: internal reproduce on A100 with stress harness.
- 2025-12-02: FP32 accumulation experiment reduces failures but latency tradeoffs noted.
- 2026-01-10: preliminary BF16 experiments promising on H100.

Contacts / escalation:
- eng-serving-runtime on Slack: #eng-serving-runtime
- Pager for P0 issues: oncall-sre@redwood-inference.com

If you read nothing else: enable KV zero-init + stable softmax + FP32 accumulation for large attention GEMMs as immediate mitigations; follow with kernel metadata contracts and scheduler numeric-mode support for longer-term robustness.
